verdict.rationale: Kimi Code Desktop and CLI are documented as agents that work in a local project folder: they edit files, run commands and verify results, so the product itself can write and run code against a user's local data. The evidence frames this as development work rather than data analysis, and the consumer assistant is only documented for file upload with question answering, not code execution. Missing for 10: documented chart/visualization generation, downloadable file outputs, a code-interpreter style data-analysis workflow in the assistant app, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can have the assistant write and run code on my data to produce charts, computed answers, and downloadable files

citations.quote: Open a local project folder in Kimi Code Desktop and let the Agent read code, edit files, run commands, and verify results through conversation.
letting it read code, edit files, execute commands, search the web, and autonomously complete development tasks.
The Kimi intelligent assistant can upload files and answer questions based on those files.
